rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice when A remains alive or exists longer than B.

example.english: I expect my grandmother to outlive my grandfather.
example.traditional: 我估我阿婆會長命過我阿爺。
example.jyutping: ngo5 gu2 ngo5 aa3 po4 wui5 coeng4 meng6 gwo3 ngo5 aa3 je4

rows.note: Use this when A survives until B's death, often with an emphatic or grim tone.

example.english: The old man manages to outlive his enemy and finally gets to rest easy.
example.traditional: 個老人家捱到個仇家死，終於可以瞓個安樂覺。
example.jyutping: go3 lou5 jan4 gaa1 ngaai4 dou3 go3 sau4 gaa1 sei2 zung1 jyu1 ho2 ji5 fan3 go3 on1 lok6 gaau3

rows.jyutping: A jung6 dak1 noi6 gwo3 B
rows.note: Use this for an object, appliance, or other thing that stays usable longer than B.

example.english: This washing machine will outlive that one, so it is much better value.
example.traditional: 呢部洗衣機用得耐過嗰部，抵買好多。
example.jyutping: ne1 bou6 sai2 ji1 gei1 jung6 dak1 noi6 gwo3 go2 bou6 dai2 maai5 hou2 do1
